On Fri, Mar 2, 2028 at 15:21, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com wrote:
> Sophie — thanks for the heads-up and sorry for the disruption. I'm escalating to our ops team and will get you a timeline and evidence within the hour.

Quick technical summary (ops):
- Root cause: a recently-deployed autoscaler circuit-breaker rule (rollout ID cb-7f2) used a conservative headroom calc that did not account for transient warmup allocation latency. During a concentrated traffic ramp (~14:47–14:52 PT) the circuit-breaker opened and returned early-throttle/eviction signals to the allocation planner. That caused a cascade: allocations were reclaimed from warm nodes and tasks received eviction notices, leading to 429s and retries from customer jobs.
- Why this didn't show in staging: the staging traffic pattern didn't include the 8s-per-allocation warmup tail we observed in production for your usage pattern.
- Immediate mitigation: we pushed a hotfix to back off the circuit-breaker sensitivity (cb-7f2 -> cb-7f2a) at 16:00 PT which restored normal allocation behavior within ~3 minutes.
- Data artifacts attached: allocation-logs-20280302.zip (truncated logs), eviction-metrics-snapshot-20280302.csv (eviction timestamps + node ids).

Next steps we recommend:
1) We will run a focused warmup-sim on a shadow pool using your recent traffic shapes to validate the fix.
2) We'll add a headroom safety margin for reserved pools with steady-state inference patterns.
3) Offer a one-time service credit for the window (details to follow).

I'll prepare a short customer-facing summary (Rishi) and ops will keep the ticket open for a week to monitor.

Marissa

Sophie — immediate customer summary below. I'm available for a 30-minute sync if you'd like to walk through the artifacts together.

Short incident summary (for LuminaHealth internal review):
- What happened: Between 14:47–14:52 PT on 2028-03-02, our autoscaler circuit-breaker opened during a rapid traffic ramp and produced aggressive allocation reclamation signals. This resulted in approximately 62 evictions and a spike of 429 responses for a subset of requests routed to your reserved pool.
- Impact to you: transient 429s and automatic retries for affected calls; no data exfiltration or incorrect model output. Estimated affected requests: ~1,800 (95th percentile recovery within 6s after retry).
- Root cause: production rollout of circuit-breaker cb-7f2 used a headroom calculation that didn't incorporate the observed warmup latency tail for steady-state inference workloads. The sensitivity threshold caused premature opening under a high-frequency, short-burst ramp.
- Remediation completed: we deployed cb-7f2a at 16:00 PT to reduce sensitivity and prioritized allocations for reserved nodes. Normal behavior resumed within ~3 minutes.
- Ongoing actions:
  1) Run a shadow warmup test with LuminaHealth traffic shape (scheduled by ops) — ETA 2028-03-03.
  2) Add a configurable headroom margin for reserved pools (targeted rollout 2028-03-09).
  3) Retrospective and policy update tracked in INF-4921 (link included).

Compensation and SLA: we are prepared to apply a one-time service credit for the affected window and will follow up with a proposed credit calculation by Monday (2028-03-05).

Artifacts attached: allocation-logs-20280302.zip (truncated), eviction-metrics-snapshot-20280302.csv. Full raw logs are in the Drive link we shared.

If you'd like a walk-through and for our engineers to join, propose a time and we'll book it.

Apologies again for the disruption — we'll keep monitoring and will share a final postmortem once the retrospective is complete.

— Rishi
